h: Tips for the slides and a full North Bay day
p: Get the most from your visit by planning a little in advance. Pack swimwear, a towel each, flip-flops for walking around and a change of warm clothes for afterwards, as the Yorkshire coast can be chilly when you step back outside. Goggles help younger swimmers and anyone braving the wave pool, and a waterproof phone pouch is useful if you want photos.

Each slide comes with its own height and safety rules, so check them as a family before you go and decide who's brave enough for what. Starting on the gentler slides and working up is a good way to build confidence. Keep the outdoor pools for later in the visit, when you've warmed up; bobbing in hot water with a cool sea breeze on your face is a lovely way to wind down.
How long to allow? Most families will want a good few hours, with breaks for a snack. If the spa is on your list, plan around it so nobody's left waiting.

North Bay has lots more to fill the rest of the day. Scarborough Open Air Theatre hosts big-name concerts in summer, and Sea Life Scarborough, at the far end of the bay, is a great add-on for younger children. In summer, Peasholm Park's famous model naval battle on the lake is a quirky local tradition that kids love.

For a walk, follow Marine Drive around the headland beneath the castle to the South Bay, with its harbour, amusements and seafront chippies. Up by the castle, St Mary's Church is where the writer Anne Brontë is buried, a quiet spot with a fascinating story.
